items.statement: Batch reconciliation throughput must not regress versus the legacy binary.
items.target: The 250,000-row benchmark fixture completes in no more than 110% of the legacy binary's measured wall-clock time on the same reference hardware.

items.statement: The reconciliation engine must be covered by automated unit tests, replacing the current manual-replay validation process.
items.target: At least 90% branch coverage on TradeReconciliationEngine and its adapters, measured in CI.

items.statement: The service must be operable by the current on-call rotation without WCF/MSMQ-specific expertise, and must preserve the existing 15-minute polling cadence.
items.target: Zero references to System.ServiceModel or System.Messaging in the ported codebase; the file-drop poll interval remains configurable, defaulting to 15 minutes.

items.statement: The service must run on a runtime that receives security patches.
items.target: .NET 8 LTS, with no dependency on any package that only supports .NET Framework.

items.statement: Each run must emit structured, machine-parseable logs indicating counts of matched, exception (by reason), input trades and input settlements, to support operational monitoring that does not exist today.
items.target: One structured log entry per run summarizing counts; no sensitive trade or settlement content (see AUD-* pattern reused in audit-feature) is required to be redacted here since this log is counts-only, not per-record.
